The directory is empty and has no existing framework or dependencies to preserve. I’ll use a dependency-free static web app so it can run entirely locally by opening `index.html` (or from any local static server), with:

1. `game.js` as a reusable rules engine: tile construction, sorting/display names, standard winning-hand decomposition, chi/pon/ron eligibility, and deterministic bot discard selection.
2. `app.js` as the browser controller: deal/play loop, user actions and claim window, automatic computer turns/claims, table rendering, and `localStorage` resume support.
3. A responsive visual table in `styles.css`, with all text in English.
4. Node’s built-in test runner to check winning-hand and claim legality independently of the UI.

House rules will be visible in the game UI and README: 136 tiles, standard four melds plus pair wins, chi/pon/ron claims, with no kan, flowers, riichi, or tournament scoring.

# Willow Table

A local, dependency-free four-player Mahjong game. Open `index.html` in a browser, or serve this folder with any static file server. Game state is stored only in the browser's `localStorage`; there are no accounts, network calls, or deployment configuration.

## House rules

- 136 standard tiles; no flowers or bonus tiles.
- You are East. East starts with 14 tiles and discards first.
- A winning hand is exactly four sets (three identical tiles or a same-suit run) and one pair. Seven pairs, thirteen orphans, and other special hands are intentionally not included.
- Ron may be claimed from any discard. Pon may be claimed from any discard. Chi is only available to the immediately next player.
- Claim precedence is Ron, then Pon, then Chi. The computer players evaluate their legal claims automatically.
- Kan, Riichi, dora, wagering, and score calculation are omitted. The hand ends in a win or exhaustive draw.

## Checks

Requires Node 18 or newer. Run:

```sh
npm test
npm run check
```

The tests cover standard hand recognition, exposed-set hand recognition, invalid hand rejection, ron eligibility, pon eligibility, and chi direction/options.

## Turn-loop rules corrected

Updated Willow Table in `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table`.

### Gameplay fixes

- Added a **Self-draw win** action for you whenever:
  - it is your discard phase, and
  - your current hand is a legal completed hand.
- The **discarder is excluded** from all claim eligibility. A player can no longer Ron, Pon, or Chi their own discarded tile.
- Claim settlement now follows the documented order:
  1. **Ron**
  2. **Pon**
  3. **Chi**
- Within the same claim priority, the winner is selected by **clockwise seat distance from the discarder**.
- A user-requested **Pon or Chi cannot override a computer player’s legal Ron**.
- Computer players are also resolved through the same priority and distance rules.

### Persistence and callback handling

- Refreshing during a computer turn resumes its pending draw/discard behavior.
- Refreshing during a claim window:
  - restores the player’s available claim controls after a computer discard;
  - resumes automatic settlement after the player’s discard;
  - automatically advances a computer discard when the player has no legal claim.
- Starting a new hand cancels the current timer and increments a generation token, so stale callbacks from the prior hand cannot alter the new hand.

### Testable turn transitions

Added:

- `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/transitions.js`

It now owns pure state transitions for drawing, discarding, self-draw validity, claim availability, claim selection, claim settlement, and applying settlements. The browser UI in `app.js` is now a thin persistence/timer/rendering adapter around those transitions.

### Regression checks added

The suite now includes checks for:

- Self-draw eligibility.
- Discarder exclusion.
- Computer Ron beating a user Pon.
- Computer Ron beating a user Chi.
- Clockwise distance resolution for equal-priority claims.
- Serialized pending claim and computer-discard states.
- Automatic no-claim continuation after a restored computer discard.
- Immutable draw and settlement transitions.

`README.md` now correctly says to launch through a local HTTP server because the game uses ES modules. For example:


Then open:

 3 | A local, dependency-free four-player Mahjong game. It uses JavaScript modules, so serve this folder from a local HTTP server rather than opening `index.html` directly. For example, from this directory run `python3 -m http.server 4330`, then visit `http://127.0.0.1:4330`. Game state is stored only in the browser's `localStorage`; there are no accounts, network calls, or deployment configuration.
 4 | 
 5 | ## House rules
 6 | 
 7 | - 136 standard tiles; no flowers or bonus tiles.
 8 | - Seats proceed clockwise as East (you), South, West, then North. East starts with 14 tiles and discards first.
 9 | - A winning hand is exactly four sets (three identical tiles or a same-suit run) and one pair. Seven pairs, thirteen orphans, and other special hands are intentionally not included.
10 | - Ron may be claimed from any discard. Pon may be claimed from any discard. Chi is only available to the immediately next player.
11 | - Claim precedence is Ron, then Pon, then Chi. Equal-priority claims are awarded clockwise from the discarder (the closest seat wins). The computer players evaluate their legal claims automatically.
12 | - Self-draw wins are available only on East’s opening 14-tile hand or immediately after drawing from the wall—not after a Pon or Chi. Kan, Riichi, dora, wagering, and score calculation are omitted. The hand ends in a win or exhaustive draw.
13 |

17 | 
18 | ```sh
19 | npm test
20 | npm run check
21 | ```

23 | The tests cover standard and exposed-set hand recognition, invalid hand rejection, ron/pon/chi eligibility, self-draw eligibility, claim priority and clockwise tie-breaking, discarder exclusion, persisted claim/discard continuation, and immutable draw/claim transitions.

content.text:
Implemented and validated the requested edge cases.

### Changes made

- Added persisted `turnStartedByDraw` round state:
  - `true` for East’s opening dealt hand.
  - `true` after a successful wall draw.
  - `false` after a discard, claim advance, Pon, or Chi.
  - Because it is part of `state`, it survives localStorage refresh automatically.

- Tightened self-draw eligibility in `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/transitions.js`:
  - A completed hand may self-draw only during its owner’s discard phase **and** when `turnStartedByDraw === true`.
  - A completed hand immediately after Pon or Chi cannot self-draw.

- Standardized seats as clockwise:
  - **East (you), South, West, North**
  - Updated `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/game.js`, `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/app.js`, `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/index.html`, CSS table positions, and `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/README.md`.

- Added defensive state/action validation:
  - Rejects unknown tile codes.
  - Rejects states with more than four physical copies of a tile across wall, hands, discards, and melds.
  - Rejects invalid exposed melds and more than four exposed melds for a player.
  - Rejects invalid Chi option indexes.
  - Invalid transitions/settlements return `null` without throwing or mutating the current round state.

- Added focused regression coverage in:
  - `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/game.test.js`

### Supported behavior now covered by checks

- Standard four-sets-plus-pair wins, including exposed meld accounting.
- Ron, Pon, and next-player-only Chi claims.
- Ron → Pon → Chi precedence and clockwise tie breaking.
- No self-claim by the discarder.
- Self-draw only on East’s opening hand or after a wall draw—not after Pon/Chi.
- Refresh-safe persisted draw-origin state.
- Valid tile-code enforcement and four-copy physical tile limits.
- Valid exposed triplets/runs, with at most four exposed melds.
- Invalid Chi selections and malformed state/action input safely leave the round unchanged.

### Validation

Passed successfully:

```sh
npm test
# 20 passing tests

npm run check
# game.js, transitions.js, and app.js syntax checks pass
```

  12: - Self-draw wins are available only on East’s opening 14-tile hand or immediately after drawing from the wall—not after a Pon or Chi. Kan, Riichi, dora, wagering, and score calculation are omitted. The hand ends in a win or exhaustive draw.

content.text: The project is a compact, dependency-free browser game with state transitions already covered by Node tests. The initial implementation renders tile buttons as immediate discards and currently has only a single last-discard display, so I’ll now read the complete UI, styling, state-transition behavior, and existing tests before changing those interaction contracts.

1 | # Willow Table
 2 | 
 3 | A local, dependency-free four-player Mahjong game. It uses JavaScript modules, so serve this folder from a local HTTP server rather than opening `index.html` directly. For example, from this directory run `python3 -m http.server 4330`, then visit `http://127.0.0.1:4330`. Game state is stored only in the browser's `localStorage`; there are no accounts, network calls, or deployment configuration.
 4 | 
 5 | ## House rules
 6 | 
 7 | - 136 standard tiles; no flowers or bonus tiles.
 8 | - Seats proceed clockwise as East (you), South, West, then North. East starts with 14 tiles and discards first.
 9 | - A winning hand is exactly four sets (three identical tiles or a same-suit run) and one pair. Seven pairs, thirteen orphans, and other special hands are intentionally not included.
10 | - Ron may be claimed from any discard. Pon may be claimed from any discard. Chi is only available to the immediately next player.
11 | - Claim precedence is Ron, then Pon, then Chi. Equal-priority claims are awarded clockwise from the discarder (the closest seat wins). The computer players evaluate their legal claims automatically.
12 | - Self-draw wins are available only on East’s opening 14-tile hand or immediately after drawing from the wall—not after a Pon or Chi. Kan, Riichi, dora, wagering, and score calculation are omitted. The hand ends in a win or exhaustive draw.
13 | 
14 | ## Checks
15 | 
16 | Requires Node 18 or newer. Run:
17 | 
18 | ```sh
19 | npm test
20 | npm run check
21 | ```
22 | 
23 | The tests cover standard and exposed-set hand recognition, invalid hand rejection, ron/pon/chi eligibility, opening/wall-draw self-draw eligibility, claim priority and clockwise tie-breaking, discarder exclusion, persisted claim/discard continuation, immutable draw/claim transitions, tile-code and four-copy limits, exposed-meld limits, and invalid Chi selections.

## Implementation plan

1. Make the table’s desktop geometry substantially shorter and keep the hand/actions within a 720px viewport; on phones, keep tile-label font sizes intact and make only the hand horizontally scrollable.
2. Replace immediate tile discard with a selected-tile state and explicit **Discard selected tile** control. Add hand navigation for Arrow keys, Home/End, Enter, and Escape, and restore meaningful focus after turn/claim changes.
3. Preserve a separate, serializable discard history for each seat so claimed discards do not disappear from the historical record; render complete histories for all four players.
4. Add an English-only Settings disclosure backed by local storage for computer pace, text size, and reduced-motion preference (default: follow the device).
5. Improve polite status announcements and use plain-English claim labels/explanations. Then run the test suite, syntax checks, and a final source inspection.

content.text:
Implemented the requested playability, responsive, accessibility, and persistence improvements.

### What changed

- **More compact desktop table**
  - Reduced desktop table felt height from 630px to 500px.
  - Tightened header, table, tile, action-area, and rule-card spacing so the hand and controls fit much better at **1280×720**.

- **Comfortable phone layout**
  - Kept normal tile-label sizing on mobile rather than shrinking it.
  - Made the player hand a horizontal scrolling strip on narrow screens.
  - Preserved a readable felt/table layout and compact opponent information.

- **Select, then discard**
  - Clicking a tile now selects it.
  - A disabled/enabled **Discard selected tile** button appears in turn controls.
  - Selected tiles have a clear visual state and `aria-pressed` state.

- **Keyboard and focus support**
  - While focus is in the hand:
    - Arrow keys navigate selected tiles.
    - `Home` / `End` select first / last tile.
    - `Enter` discards the selected tile.
    - `Escape` clears selection.
  - Focus moves back to the hand when the player’s turn begins and to claim choices when a claim decision is needed.
  - Settings controls retain their native keyboard behavior.

- **Accessibility**
  - Turn and claim messages remain politely announced through the existing live region, now with `aria-atomic="true"`.
  - Claim buttons now explain their meaning in plain English:
    - “Ron — win with this discard”
    - “Pon — make a matching triple”
    - “Chi — make a run with …”
    - “Pass — do not claim”
  - Added visible focus indicators.

- **Settings panel with local persistence**
  - Added a local, English-only Settings panel:
    - Computer turns: Slow / Normal / Fast
    - Tile text: Standard / Large
    - Reduced motion: Follow device / Reduce motion / Full motion
  - Preferences save in `localStorage` under `willow-table-preferences-v1`.
  - “Follow device” honors `prefers-reduced-motion`.

- **Full discard histories**
  - Every seat now has a collapsible complete discard history.
  - Claimed discards remain in history even though they are removed from the active discard pile.
  - Existing saved games are upgraded in memory by initializing their history from existing discards.

- **Test coverage**
  - Added a test confirming a discard remains in history after it is claimed.

Implemented the keyboard-selection and focus fixes.

### Fixed

- **End/Home/arrow focus no longer falls back to the first tile**
  - Replaced the faulty `element.focus() || fallback.focus()` behavior.
  - Focus now explicitly targets the indexed tile first and only uses the first tile if that indexed element does not exist.

- **Selection now tracks a physical hand position**
  - Replaced tile-code selection with a selected hand index.
  - Duplicate tiles are independently selectable.
  - Only the chosen duplicate receives the selected visual/ARIA state.
  - Arrow navigation moves across actual tile positions and wraps naturally.

- **Escape behavior**
  - `Escape` clears the selected tile.
  - Focus remains on the currently focused hand tile.

- **Focus preservation during computer updates**
  - The renderer records whether focus is in:
    - Settings, or
    - a discard-history panel.
  - Computer turns no longer force focus away from Settings.
  - Open discard histories are restored after re-rendering, and their summary regains focus when it was active.

### Added coverage

Added dependency-free tests in:

- `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/hand-controls.test.js`

The tests cover:

- Duplicate tile navigation by physical position.
- Home, End, arrow movement, and wrapping.
- Focus-protection behavior for Settings and discard history.

Supporting pure helpers are in:

- `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/hand-controls.js`

Updated `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/README.md` with:

- Select-then-discard behavior.
- Arrow, Home, End, Enter, and Escape controls.

content.text:
## Completed

Implemented local completed-hand history and resilient persistence for Willow Table.

### Added session history
- Records completed hands once using a persistent hand ID, including after refresh.
- Retains the newest **30** hands.
- Shows:
  - Outcome: win or draw
  - Winner
  - Finish time
  - Turn count
- Includes simple totals for completed hands, wins, and draws.
- Filters: all hands, wins, or draws.
- Each history item supports a local personal note (up to 280 characters).
- No money, wagering, or tournament scoring was introduced.

### Restart and completion behavior
- **New hand** now asks for confirmation when an unfinished hand is active.
- Discarded unfinished hands are not added to history.
- Completed hands are safely deduplicated, including when loading a previously completed saved hand.

### Persistence hardening
- Added `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/persistence.js`.
- Browser storage is guarded against:
  - unavailable storage,
  - blocked storage,
  - malformed JSON,
  - write failures.
- The game remains playable in the current tab when storage is unavailable, with an explicit status message.
- Damaged, invalid, or obsolete saved rounds now result in a clear status message and a fresh hand rather than a blank/broken screen.

### Round validation fixes
Updated `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/transitions.js`:
- `isValidRound` now safely rejects a `null` player instead of throwing.
- Claim-phase states now require:
  - a valid `lastDiscarder`,
  - a valid `lastDiscard`,
  - that the discarder’s current last discard matches `lastDiscard`.

### Backup and restore
Added versioned JSON backup/restore:
- Backup includes current hand, preferences, completed-hand history, and notes.
- Restore validates the entire payload before changing any local data.
- Restore asks for confirmation before replacing the current hand, settings, history, and notes.
- Invalid/unsupported backup files leave existing data untouched and show an explanatory message.

### UI and documentation
Updated:
- `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/index.html`
- `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/styles.css`
- `/Users/andychen/Documents/ChatGPT/Vibe Code/willow-table/README.md`

### Tests added
- Null player and malformed claim-window validation.
- History deduplication and 30-item cap.
- Valid and damaged backup payload handling.
- Unavailable storage behavior.

### Validation run
All checks pass:

```text
npm test        # 27 passing tests
npm run check   # syntax checks pass, including persistence.js
git diff --check
```

<user_input mode="act">I found a few issues in review. Searching result text for the word draw marks self-draw wins as Draw; please store an explicit result kind and winning seat instead. Backup history currently accepts arbitrary outcome strings and duplicate IDs, and imported round metadata and discardHistory are not fully checked. Validate these fields, enforce real 136-tile round inventories and phase-appropriate hand sizes at the persistence boundary, and render imported text safely. A failed storage write after restore must not say the backup was saved locally. Please preserve typed notes and focus while computer turns render. The new controller also lost the explanatory claim labels and the fallback that focuses the first hand tile at the start of my turn; restore those. Add targeted regressions and a deterministic full-round simulation that exercises draws, discards and claims, checks tile conservation, and confirms hands terminate. Keep all existing features working.</user_input>

## Plan

I’ll audit the current persistence schema, round model, render/focus behavior, and tests against each review finding. Then I’ll tighten the validated boundary (including explicit completion metadata, canonical tile inventory and phase hand counts), repair UI focus/claim guidance, add a deterministic end-to-end simulation, and run the full suite plus syntax/diff checks.

content.text:
## Completed

Implemented the review fixes across the controller, transition state, persistence boundary, and tests.

### Result metadata and history
- Replaced display-text inference (`/draw/i`) with explicit round fields:
  - `resultKind`: `"win"` or `"draw"`
  - `winnerSeat`: seat index or `null` for draws
- History now records result kind and winner from these fields, so self-draw wins are no longer misclassified as draws.
- History validation now rejects:
  - arbitrary outcome strings,
  - duplicate hand IDs,
  - invalid winner/outcome combinations.

### Backup/restore hardening
- Bumped backup schema to **version 2** because explicit completion metadata is now required.
- Added `isValidSavedRound()` at the persistence boundary. Imported/saved rounds now require:
  - a valid hand ID, turn count, message/result metadata, and completion timestamp,
  - a complete canonical **136-tile inventory**,
  - valid per-tile multiplicity,
  - phase-appropriate concealed-hand sizes,
  - valid `discardHistory` tiles with all visible discards represented in history,
  - explicit, consistent win/draw metadata.
- Invalid/old backups are rejected before replacing session state.
- Restore now reports:
  - **“Backup restored locally”** only when all storage writes succeed.
  - **“Backup restored for this tab, but browser storage is unavailable.”** when writing fails.

### UI resilience and accessibility

1 | # Willow Table
 2 | 
 3 | A local, dependency-free four-player Mahjong game. It uses JavaScript modules, so serve this folder from a local HTTP server rather than opening `index.html` directly. For example, from this directory run `python3 -m http.server 4330`, then visit `http://127.0.0.1:4330`. Game state is stored only in the browser's `localStorage`; there are no accounts, network calls, or deployment configuration.
 4 | 
 5 | ## House rules
 6 | 
 7 | - 136 standard tiles; no flowers or bonus tiles.
 8 | - Seats proceed clockwise as East (you), South, West, then North. East starts with 14 tiles and discards first.
 9 | - A winning hand is exactly four sets (three identical tiles or a same-suit run) and one pair. Seven pairs, thirteen orphans, and other special hands are intentionally not included.
10 | - Ron may be claimed from any discard. Pon may be claimed from any discard. Chi is only available to the immediately next player.
11 | - Claim precedence is Ron, then Pon, then Chi. Equal-priority claims are awarded clockwise from the discarder (the closest seat wins). The computer players evaluate their legal claims automatically.
12 | - Self-draw wins are available only on East’s opening 14-tile hand or immediately after drawing from the wall—not after a Pon or Chi. Kan, Riichi, dora, wagering, and score calculation are omitted. The hand ends in a win or exhaustive draw.
13 | 
14 | ## Playing controls and preferences
15 | 
16 | - Select a tile, then use **Discard selected tile** to throw it. Each physical tile has its own selection, including duplicate tiles.
17 | - With focus in your hand, use **Arrow keys** to move the selection, **Home** or **End** for the first or last tile, **Enter** to discard the selected tile, and **Escape** to clear the selection while keeping focus in the hand.
18 | - The Settings panel saves its choices locally: computer turn pace (slow, normal, or fast), standard or large tile text, and reduced motion (follow the device by default, reduce, or full motion).
19 | - Every seat has a collapsible full discard history. The game preserves focus in Settings and an open discard history while computer turns update the table.
20 | - The local session panel retains the newest 30 completed hands with outcome, winner, finish time, turn count, optional personal notes, filters, and simple win/draw totals. Unfinished hands are never included.
21 | - Download a versioned JSON backup of the current hand, preferences, completed-hand history, and notes. Restore validates it before asking to replace local data. If browser storage is blocked or unavailable, the game still plays in the current tab and says so.
22 | 
23 | ## Checks
24 | 
25 | Requires Node 18 or newer. Run:
26 | 
27 | ```sh
28 | npm test
29 | npm run check
30 | ```
31 | 
32 | The tests cover standard and exposed-set hand recognition, invalid hand rejection, ron/pon/chi eligibility, opening/wall-draw self-draw eligibility, claim priority and clockwise tie-breaking, discarder exclusion, persisted claim/discard continuation, immutable draw/claim transitions, tile-code and four-copy limits, exposed-meld limits, invalid Chi selections, discard-history retention, duplicate-tile position navigation, and protected-focus behavior.

content.text: The transition layer already provides authoritative legal human-claim detection and settlement. The required behavior is therefore: after any discard, schedule automatic settlement only when East has no legal claim; otherwise leave the claim window open until East explicitly claims or passes. I’ll centralize that policy and the generation-guarded timeout lifecycle in a DOM-free controller, wire `app.js` through it (including new-hand cancellation), and add controlled-timer tests for all three requested cases.
